instruction:
Create the task list that breaks down the implementation work.

Before writing tasks, check design.md for Open Questions. If any of them
would change what gets built, resolve them with the user first - do not
bake an unstated assumption into the task list.

**IMPORTANT: Follow the template below for tracked tasks.** The apply phase parses
checkbox format to track progress. A box holding only `x` counts as done,
upper or lower case and with any spacing, so `- [ x]` is done too. Every
other marker, including `- [~]`, `- [-]` and an empty `- []`, reads as
unfinished. A line with no checkbox is not tracked at all.

Guidelines:
- Group related tracked tasks under ## numbered headings
- Each tracked task MUST be a checkbox: `- [ ] X.Y Task description`
- Tasks should be small enough to complete in one session
- Order tasks by dependency (what must be done first?)
- Track implementation and verification work that can be completed before
  archive. If the requested workflow includes archive or work that requires
  this change to be archived, preserve those steps as plain bullets in an
  optional `## Workflow follow-up` section at the end of tasks.md. These
  bullets are reference information outside tracked task progress.
- Each task MUST state how to verify completion (a test, command,
  observable behavior, or delivered artifact). Put the verification in
  that task's checkbox description. Use a separate verification task only
  when it checks broader integration or system behavior that spans
  multiple implementation tasks.
- Each task group MUST land the tests and documentation its own work
  calls for. Do NOT collect testing or documentation into a final group -
  when a late group first exercises work from an early one, the failures
  cascade back through every group in between and force rework. A group
  whose work calls for neither, such as scaffolding or dependency setup,
  carries neither. A final group is for integration checks only, not for
  the tests and docs an earlier group owed.

Example:
```
# Tasks

## 1. Setup

- [ ] 1.1 Create new module structure and verify expected files are present
- [ ] 1.2 Add dependencies to package.json and verify package installation succeeds

## 2. Core Implementation

- [ ] 2.1 Implement data export function and verify the export test passes
- [ ] 2.2 Add CSV formatting utilities and verify unit tests cover quoting and delimiters
- [ ] 2.3 Document the export API in docs/export.md and verify the documented command runs as written
```

When applicable, append workflow follow-up as plain bullets, for example:
```
## Workflow follow-up

- Archive the change after the project's review requirements are satisfied.
- Verify the archived result.
```

Reference specs for what needs to be built, design for how to build it.
context:
Project: Uplift, a personal local/offline covert civilization simulation to share with friends. Inspirations include Banks (Inversions, Matter, Use of Weapons / Special Circumstances), Saberhagen (Brother Assassin) and Strugatsky (Hard to Be a God). Target: 2019 Intel Core i7 MacBook Pro, 16 GB RAM, 60 FPS. Runtime and tests use zero external API keys or cloud inference.

Authority and navigation:
- DESIGN_NOTES.md holds the owner pillars P1–P5, rules spine R1–R8, system graph, status index, Where-facts-live table and design dispositions. Read it and notes/inbox.md before proposals. Preserve unresolved inbox inputs and owner exemplars verbatim. Design is living and revisable.
- openspec/roadmap.yaml owns ordered work, dependencies, milestones, parked entries and revisit triggers. Never infer readiness merely from a status label.
- Fine-grained distant design lives in indexed design/ files; DESIGN_NOTES.md owns the summaries. No fixed engine epoch count exists. Epoch and Era are synonyms; the default seven-rung campaign is planned data, not a shipped blueprint.
- Root and scoped README/AGENTS describe shipped code. Read the target section's guide and update both files when capabilities change. Version pins, engine compatibility, scripts and overrides come from package.json; .nvmrc selects Node. Do not duplicate dated version or CVE tables.
- New live change citations belong in openspec/, DESIGN_NOTES.md and design/. Historical tracked reviews are retained evidence, not rewritten as live guidance.

Shipped foundation:
- Pure domain schemas, EpochModuleRegistry, SeededRandom, state slices, waypoint kinematics, human-paced cognitive scheduling, WorldEffect reducers and legacy/save contracts exist. Additional registry kinds do not imply authored playable economies, rivals or correspondence. Emergency and orbital reducers already exist.
- Application coordinates the simulation and pure render frames. Browser composition uses one page/canvas, a proving pack, development waypoint controls, stage switching and the F3 stage/wardrobe lab. Browser telemetry and saves are in memory; saved lab JSON is not a launch source yet.
- Infrastructure supplies NDJSON telemetry, rolling compaction, rotation and file saves. The browser is not wired to disk telemetry. The active size threshold triggers compaction rather than imposing a hard cap; compacted storage uses priority eviction. Operational details and recovery live in src/infrastructure/README.md and the uplift-debug skill. Guarded loopback HTTP routes and their tests are shipped.
- The campaign, direct movement/use, text/paging, local generation, audio, watches, eval runner and advanced content remain planned. Their numbers, exemplars and contract names belong in DESIGN_NOTES.md and its indexed feature files, not repeated here.

Engineering:
- interfaces may depend on application, domain, infrastructure and content; application and infrastructure depend inward on domain. Non-scene content depends on domain; content/scene may depend on interfaces/three, domain and three. Domain has no outward project dependencies, DOM/WebGL or model runtime. Preserve the full root/scoped layer rules and architecture assertions.
- Strict TypeScript and zero implicit/explicit any apply to source and tests. Domain and content forbid ambient randomness/time; use injected SeededRandom and clocks. Keep content identifiers and tuning data outside domain/application. Preserve deterministic pure reducers and immutable inputs.
- Use the default checkout, including apply; no isolated worktree without owner request. Inspect status and preserve unrelated work. Run npm run verify after each task. It runs concurrent format/lint/types/tests; verify:serial remains available. Reference budgets are measured targets, not wall-clock assertions. Existing HTTP tests need loopback access. The commit hook runs lint-staged then full verification without staging unrelated files.

Workflow:
- Project skills belong in .agents/skills/, never .cursor/skills/. Root AGENTS links all ten workflows. uplift-review-gates is authoritative for task sizing, G1–G6, findings and document integrity; root-and-branch-review governs periodic deep review. Use uplift-design-notes for design inputs and uplift-debug for telemetry diagnosis.
- Preserve three independent proposal auditors, two reviewers per task and six delivery reviewers, with high reasoning, medium-to-high model briefs. Limited slots mean waves, not fewer reviews. Findings require independent verification, disposition and retained evidence. Record missing evidence honestly.
- Owner review follows proposal validation; implementation starts only on apply. Owner approval precedes each commit and archive; never push without instruction. Until ledger commands ship, use the active proposal finding inventory for bootstrap G5 evidence.
- Before cutting or moving documents, map every paragraph/block to retained meaning or explicit superseding authority; two independent fidelity/coherence passes precede cuts. Root AGENTS targets about 900 words, ceiling 1,050; this context stays below 1,500. The roughly 14,000-word DESIGN_NOTES target is aspirational; its larger baseline is accepted. Engineering-rule splitting remains deferred until M1 delivery.
rules: One task is one green Conventional Commit touching at most three source/tooling files plus tests, with related docs in the task. More than eight tasks or three runtime layers needs explicit justification or a split; do not enforce the superseded fixed 4-6 count.

Every task includes its Verify command and intended Conventional Commit message; order inward-out where relevant so intermediate commits compile and pass npm run verify. Include a closing review task to record unplanned fixes.

Per task: run targeted verification and npm run verify, obtain two independent reviews with high reasoning, medium-to-high model briefs (correctness/logic/edges/performance; architecture/spec/types/coverage), verify findings, fix confirmed issues and rerun checks. Inspect the scoped diff and pause for owner approval before commit or marking completion.
Complete G1-G6 evidence with honest gaps; use the bootstrap finding inventory until checked ledger commands ship. Do not run nonexistent commands or claim missing reconciliation passed.

Before delivery/archive obtain all six independent reviews with high reasoning, medium-to-high model briefs: adversarial; architecture/adherence; performance; testing; logic/simulation integrity; design coherence. Reconcile findings, verify paired guides, run npm run verify and obtain owner archive instruction. Never automatically push.
